clue.text: Composer very into melodies with keys oddly used

indicators.note: the word very is put into the word for melodies

parts.note: strains are tunes or melodies

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of keys are used, the first and third

explanation.surface: A musician setting very tuneful melodies with a curious choice of keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts V inside STRAINS; 'oddly used' takes K and Y, the first and third letters of 'keys'.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian-born writer of The Rite of Spring, a famous twentieth-century musician.

clue.text: In capital city, high Anglican, initially, is bishop?

parts.note: tall means high

indicators.note: only the first letter of Anglican is taken

parts.note: a bishop is one who has a see, his diocese

explanation.surface: A senior High Church clergyman questioned about his post in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic step: being a bishop means having a see. 'initially' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallahassee is the state capital of Florida.

clue.text: What gives one's height and age in turn

indicators.note: the word for age goes in the word for turn

parts.note: to turn is to alter or change
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A record showing how tall someone is and how old, taken in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reads as 'in sequence', but 'in' is the container signal and 'turn' the word being altered.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is an instrument measuring elevation above sea level.

clue.text: Extract reportedly found under the counter

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for extract is spoken

parts.note: to elicit is to draw out or extract

explanation.surface: An extract supposedly discovered beneath a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals the homophone of ELICIT. Goods sold 'under the counter' are traded secretly or unlawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Under-the-counter dealings are unlawful and hidden, just as forbidden trade is.

clue.text: Fellow-member board included in second handbook

indicators.note: the word for board is included in the others

parts.note: a companion is a guidebook or handbook, as in The Oxford Companion
a table is a board

explanation.surface: A colleague's board was put into the next edition of a manual.
explanation.walkthrough: A companion is also the name for a reference handbook, as in The Oxford Companion to English Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable companion is literally a horse from the same stable, figuratively a colleague from the same organisation.

clue.text: London copper — one working on trains? ().

definitions.meaning: a Scotland Yard detective, from the Metropolitan Police headquarters
a worker in a railway yard, marshalling carriages

explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotland Yard officer is a 'Yard man'; a railway yard worker is also one.

clue.text: Sound beating repeatedly delivered by karate chop

indicators.note: the letters are delivered by, carried within, the words karate chop

explanation.surface: A rhythmic thudding noise produced by a martial-arts blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'karate' and the start of 'chop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation is a noise bouncing back again and again off a surface.

clue.text: Country familiar to a Cockney

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang ... plate means mate, a familiar friend

explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners famous for rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation is in East Asia; a 'china' is a mate in Cockney rhyming slang, from 'china plate'.

clue.text: Plant found in neat study

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
to eye is to look at or study

explanation.surface: A flower discovered in a tidy office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy; it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a common white wild flower.

clue.text: Many small vessels left all of it at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned everything on the ocean, a picture of boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges L, ALL and OFIT; the sea image also suits the boats of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a fleet of little boats or ships sailing together.

clue.text: People welcoming popular foreign dramatist

indicators.note: the word for people takes in, welcomes, the word for popular

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A nation giving a warm reception to a well-liked playwright from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' is the container signal: the people hold the popular piece inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a seventeenth-century French tragedian, so a playwright from abroad to an English solver.

clue.text: Jack's coat that's laid down to cover road

definitions.text: that's laid down to cover road

parts.note: a jack tar, or simply a tar, is a sailor
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

explanation.surface: A sailor's raincoat spread out over the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and tar are both old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the asphalt surfacing material spread on streets and runways.

clue.text: Pop article found in French daily

indicators.note: the article is found inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: Le Monde is a daily newspaper in France
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A feature on popular music appearing in a Paris newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts A inside LE MONDE. 'Pop' looks like pop music; it is the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and a lemon-flavoured fizzy drink is one example.

clue.text: In personal records, head of government can upset VIPs

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the word for personal records

parts.note: diaries are personal records

indicators.note: only the first letter of government is taken
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Diaries reveal that a leader of the government might cause offence to important people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, where turning the can upside down reads it backwards; 'In' places everything inside the records.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignitaries are very important people holding high office.

clue.text: This philosopher is talking jargon

indicators.note: talking signals that the word for jargon is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: cant is the jargon of a particular group

explanation.surface: A thinker who speaks in specialist gobbledygook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' signals the homophone of CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century German thinker behind the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Applied know-how to find the only cog that needs replacing

indicators.note: the letters need to be replaced, put back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A mechanic's practical skill finds the single cog in the machine that is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that needs replacing' rearranges THEONLYCOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology is scientific knowledge put to practical use.

clue.text: Characters smirking about diminutive island race

indicators.note: the word for smirking goes about the race

parts.note: leering means smirking
TT is the short form of the Tourist Trophy, a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: People sneering at a small race of islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man TT is a famous motorbike road race; 'about' means the smirking word goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettering is written or printed letters, that is, characters.

clue.text: Jeans, for example, or one smart ensemble

indicators.note: an ensemble is a set of things put together, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Denim trousers, or perhaps a single chic outfit, as fashion choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensemble' rearranges ORONESMART. Jeans looks like denim; it is Sir James Jeans, the British stargazer and writer on the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir James Jeans was a noted British scientist who studied stars and the universe.

clue.text: Bothers, after one's dropped out to get fine degrees?

indicators.note: the letters for one's are dropped out of the word

parts.note: nuisances are bothers
one is I, and 's is is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: Annoyances persist after a student quits, in the hope of a good degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped out' removes IS from NUISANCES. 'Degrees' looks academic; the question mark flags degrees of difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuances are subtle shades of difference in meaning or tone.

clue.text: No problem for a showjumper

definitions.meaning: a no is a denial or turning down
a horse's stopping at a fence, which costs penalty faults

explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is a rejection; a horse balking at a fence is also called this in showjumping.

clue.text: Poor article has no conclusion

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, its conclusion

parts.note: a thing is an object or article

explanation.surface: A weak newspaper piece that never reaches an ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no conclusion' drops G from THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin can mean meagre or feeble, as in a thin excuse.

clue.text: Brew made with rare type of rum

indicators.note: to brew is to concoct, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A drink concocted from an unusual kind of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brew' rearranges MADE and RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara rum comes from the Demerara region of Guyana.

clue.text: Model partner putting cards on the table

definitions.text: partner putting cards on the table
definitions.meaning: in bridge, the declarer's partner lays the hand face up

explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's mannequin is a model; in bridge the exposed hand and its holder share the name.

clue.text: Obscure film introducing unknown

indicators.note: the film comes first, introducing the unknown that follows

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An art-house movie presenting a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie; it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Misty means blurred or vague, hard to see clearly.

clue.text: Excited of late, being in such a state before one's birthday

definitions.text: in such a state before one's birthday

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are agitated

explanation.surface: Someone has been thrilled lately, as people are before a birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' rearranges OFLATE. The birthday is the day of birth itself, before which one is unborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Before being born a baby is a fetus, so its condition is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Gum Mum used with glue in short supply

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to stick is to glue

explanation.surface: A mother using an adhesive sparingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short supply' drops K from STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from a Mediterranean tree, used as a chewing resin and adhesive.

clue.text: Give encouragement without being physically present

definitions.meaning: to put heart into someone, a verb
as two words, present in thought though absent in body

explanation.definitionFit: To inspirit is to hearten; being with someone 'in spirit' is being with them only in thought.

clue.text: Timeless toy repeatedly making a comeback

definitions.text: Timeless toy repeatedly making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the letters are read backwards
the remaining letters are written down twice
without T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A classic plaything that keeps returning to fashion, or keeps coming back up its string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' takes T from TOY to leave OY; 'repeatedly' doubles it; 'making a comeback' reverses OYOY.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning disc on a string is a perennial plaything that keeps returning to the hand.

clue.text: Oriental expert alone comprehends one new point

indicators.note: comprehends means includes, so the word for alone takes in the next pieces

parts.note: solo means alone
I is the Roman numeral one
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A specialist in the East, working by himself, grasps a fresh argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehends' means takes in, so the word for alone surrounds the one and the new before the point follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinologist studies Chinese language and culture, China being in the East.
